To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electron spin resonance spectra of single crystals of high-spin hæmoglobin compounds are very similar to those of single crystals of myoglobin compounds.
the g-values of the hæmoprotein spectra are: 6·0 for ferrimyoglobin, 5·6 for ferri-hæmaglobin and 5·4 for ferro-hæmaglobine.
the unpaired electron in hæmin and in high-spin hæmoprotein compounds is localized in the hæm ring, and the spin density on the iron is about 0.3.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the electron spin resonance spectra of the hæmoprotein compounds, hæmoglobin, myoglobin, cytochrome C, catalase and peroxidase, and the prosthetic group compounds, hæmin and hæmatin, in the temperature range 300° K–4.2°K.
the electron spin resonance spectrum of the hæmoprotein group in the hæmoglobin molecule and the effect of the protein structure on the electron spin resonance spectra.

a study of the electron spin structure of hæmoprotein compounds at low temperatures and the correlation of this structure with the chemical, optical, electronic, and magnetic properties of these compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the high-spin ferrihæmoprotein compounds the electron spin resonance spectra are very similar to those obtained in high-spin ferric salts.

in hæmoglobin compounds the g-values of the high-spin ferri-compound (g = 6.0) and of the high-spin ferric compound (g = 2.0) can be observed, whereas in hæmoprotein compounds containing the prosthetic group porphin (e.g., chlorophyll) no electron spin resonance spectrum is observed.

the electron spin resonance spectrum of the high-spin ferric hæmoprotein compounds is a single broad line with a width at half height of the order of 1000 G, and with a g-value which varies from g = 4 to g = 2 depending on the state of the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron spin resonance spectra of hæmin, hæmatin and hæmoglobin are very similar and the g-values vary from g = 1.98 to g = 5.5 in all three compounds.

the electron spin resonance spectra of the hæmoprotein molecules are determined by the interaction between the unpaired electrons and the paramagnetic ions of the metal ion and of the hæmin molecule itself, and that the spectra of hæmoprotiens in aqueous solution at low temperatures are determined by the interactions of the unpaired electrons with the metal ions, with the hæm group and with the protein.
the g-values for the high-spin ferric hæmoprotein compounds are g1 = 2·0, g⊥ = 6·0.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now make measurements on a single crystal of hæmoprotein and get a very detailed picture of the electron structure of the hæmoprotien.

the electron spin resonance spectrum of the hæmoprotein hæmoglobin has the same g-values as the hæmochromogen hæmin, which suggests that the hæm group in hæmoglobin may be in the same oxidation state and electronic configuration as it is in hæmin.
the electron spin resonance spectra of hæmoglobins and myoglobins at 170°, 77°, 20°, and 4.2 K show a well-defined variation in g-values, which are characteristic of high-spin ferric iron.
